long_biography.plain_text:
Machinery became central to American industrialist Dennis Washington's working life immediately after high school. In Alaska, he began by greasing equipment and advanced to operating a floating crane. Returning to Montana, he rose to vice-president of a construction company before borrowing to establish his own business.

His first contract required cutting a parking area into the rocky summit of Glacier National Park. Forest-road work prepared him for larger highway projects, and the business became Montana's largest contractor within five years. With Phyllis Washington, he established a family foundation in 1988 focused on education, health, community service and the arts.
